briefing.summary: Strongly bullish momentum following a powerful dual catalyst day on Aug 12: (1) July CPI came in cooler than expected at 2.7% YoY headline (vs 2.8% expected), cementing September rate cut expectations to ~90% probability, and (2) US-China tariff truce extended 90 days to Nov 10, avoiding escalation from 30% to 145%. S&P 500 closed at record 6,445.76 (+1.13%), Nasdaq at record 21,681.90 (+1.39%), Dow +483 pts to 44,458.61. All 11 sectors closed green. Aug 13 is a continuation/digestion day — Dow jumped another 450+ pts, S&P and Nasdaq logged back-to-back records (up ~0.3% and ~0.1% respectively). Key risk: PPI data on Aug 14 could reverse sentiment if hot. Oil bearish (EIA forecast sub-$60 by Q4, OPEC+ unwinding cuts). Gold near record highs ~$3,488. 10Y yield fell 4bps to 4.25%. Treasury Secretary Bessent called for 150-175bps of cuts. Small caps (Russell 2000) surging on rate sensitivity — up 2.9% in August, 7.3% for the full month. CoreWeave -18% on guidance cut is a notable AI infrastructure crack.

sections.title: Geopolitics
sections.content: US-China tariff truce extended 90 days on Aug 11-12, keeping tariffs at 30% on Chinese imports (vs potential 145% escalation). This was a major relief rally catalyst alongside CPI. Trump-Putin Alaska summit scheduled for Aug 15 regarding Ukraine — Trump dropped ceasefire demand in favor of 'Peace Agreement' approach. European leaders cautious. Defense spending remains elevated globally — Elbit Systems reporting 21% YoY revenue growth driven by Israel/NATO demand. Geopolitical risk temporarily suppressed but not resolved.

sections.title: Macro
sections.content: July CPI released Aug 12: headline +0.2% MoM / +2.7% YoY (below 2.8% consensus). Core CPI +0.3% MoM / +3.1% YoY (in-line, but accelerating from 2.9% in June — fastest since Feb). Tariff impact visible in household furnishings (+0.7% MoM), core commodities inflation (+1.2% YoY, fastest in 2+ years). Fed rate cut expectations surged: September cut fully priced (~90%), October cut probability jumped to 67%. Treasury Secretary Bessent publicly called for 150-175bps of total cuts. 10Y yield fell to 4.25%, 2Y fell to 3.73%. PPI due Aug 14 — the next inflection point. S&P 500 Q2 earnings: 83% beat rate, +10.6% YoY aggregate operating earnings. GDP strong. Unemployment low but moderating.

sections.title: Corporate
sections.content: Key Aug 13 earnings: Brinker International (EAT) blowout Q4 — comp sales +21.3%, Chili's +23.7%, revenue $1.45B vs $1.20B PY, $400M buyback. Elbit Systems (ESLT) Q2 — revenues +21% YoY, EPS +55%. Performance Food Group (PFGC) FY2025 record $63B revenue, EBITDA +19.9%, US Foods merger inquiry disclosed. Global-e Online (GLBE) Q2 revenue +28% to $214.9M, first GAAP profitability. CAVA cut same-store guidance to 4-6% from 6-8%, stock -16.6%. CoreWeave (CRWV) -18% on guidance cut. Paramount Skydance (PSKY) +37% on $7.7B UFC deal momentum. Apple jumped on Bloomberg AI comeback report. Circle IPO priced above range at $37. Hudbay Minerals (HBM) strong Q2 with significant free cash flow.

sections.title: TechAI
sections.content: AI infrastructure spending massive but cracks emerging. CoreWeave cut 2025 revenue guidance ($5.15-5.35B to $5.05-5.15B) due to third-party data center delays — stock -18%, signaling execution risk. Hyperscaler capex (MSFT, GOOG, AMZN, META) remains robust. Nvidia Blackwell ramp strong, approaching $50B data center revenue quarter. AMD inked OpenAI deal. SOX index +34.5% YTD. Apple announced ambitious AI product roadmap Aug 13 (Bloomberg): tabletop robot (2027), smart speaker with display (2026), lifelike Siri. Analog semiconductor super-cycle gaining momentum — ADI and peers surging. 50% copper tariff benefits domestic chip supply chain.

sections.title: Energy
sections.content: Bearish oil setup dominates. EIA Aug 12 STEO forecasts Brent below $60/bbl by Q4 2025, averaging ~$50 in 2026. OPEC+ unwinding 2.2mb/d voluntary cuts by September — a year ahead of schedule. WTI in low-to-mid $60s. US production at all-time high near 13.6mb/d. Oil fell 1.6% on Aug 13. Supply glut building. Gold near record highs ~$3,488/oz, benefiting from rate cut expectations and geopolitical hedging. Copper volatile after 50% tariff — two-tier market benefits FCX (domestic), hurts SCCO (importer).

sections.title: Policy
sections.content: Five major policy threads: (1) Trump's 50% copper import tariff effective Aug 1 — creates winners/losers. (2) US-China 90-day tariff extension signed Aug 11 — prevents escalation, markets rallied. Average effective tariff rate at 10.55%, China at 39.2%. (3) CMS Medicare Advantage rate guidance pressuring managed care stocks. (4) Treasury Sec Bessent publicly pushing for 150-175bps of total cuts — unusually aggressive political pressure on Fed. (5) Trump-Putin Alaska summit Aug 15 could move defense/energy. Core commodities inflation accelerating (+1.2% YoY), suggesting tariff passthrough happening but controlled.

recommendations.thesis: EAT reported one of the strongest restaurant quarters in years on Aug 13 pre-market. Traffic-driven growth (+16% Chili's traffic) is the highest-quality comp driver — not just pricing. 2-year sales growth of +39% shows sustainable momentum. $400M buyback provides EPS support floor. In a market where rate cut expectations boost consumer discretionary and all 11 sectors closed green the prior day, a company demonstrating genuine traffic growth commands premium multiple expansion. The Dow gained another 450+ pts on Aug 13, providing strong market tailwind.
recommendations.catalyst: Blowout Q4 earnings: comp sales +21.3%, Chili's traffic +16%, revenue $1.45B (+21% YoY), restaurant margin 17.8%, $400M buyback authorized. Post-earnings momentum in record-setting broad market.

recommendations.thesis: CoreWeave's guidance cut is the first major crack in the AI infrastructure narrative. For a stock priced for flawless execution, even a modest trim framed as 'timing shift' destroyed confidence. Third-party construction delays suggest systemic capacity constraint issues, not company-specific. The broad market rally actually makes CRWV's underperformance more painful — investors rotating to higher-conviction names. Stock eventually fell 50%+ from highs over subsequent months. Institutional selling continues for days after a guidance cut of this magnitude on a recently-IPO'd name.
recommendations.catalyst: Revenue guidance cut from $5.15-5.35B to $5.05-5.15B due to third-party data center construction delays. Operating income guidance disappointed. Already -18% but selling pressure likely continues as growth funds rebalance.

recommendations.thesis: When a high-multiple fast-casual darling cuts same-store guidance for the first time, the de-rating is typically multi-day as growth fund managers exit positions. SSS of 2.1% vs 6-8% guidance range represents dramatic deceleration that questions the entire growth thesis. The stock traded at extreme premium to restaurant peers, making downside asymmetric. Even after 16.6% drop, likely hasn't fully repriced to new growth trajectory. Analyst downgrades follow over 1-3 days. After-hours recovery to $84.50 may provide short entry on Aug 13 open.
recommendations.catalyst: First-ever guidance reduction: same-store sales cut to 4-6% from 6-8%. SSS decelerated to just 2.1%. Stock already -16.6% but institutional growth fund rebalancing continues multi-day.

recommendations.thesis: Dual catalyst of cooler CPI + US-China trade truce creates ideal small-cap environment. Small caps are more rate-sensitive (higher leverage = more benefit from lower borrowing costs), more domestically focused (trade truce reduces uncertainty), and more economically sensitive (rate cuts signal easier financial conditions). Russell 2000 surged 7.3% in August — best monthly performance of the year. Rotation from mega-cap tech to small caps is multi-week theme. Bessent calling for 150-175bps provides political tailwind. If PPI soft tomorrow, theme accelerates.
recommendations.catalyst: September rate cut at 90% probability. Russell 2000 most rate-sensitive major index. Already +2.9% in August (outperforming S&P). Valuation discount to large caps widest since dot-com. Trade truce reduces uncertainty for domestically-focused small caps.

recommendations.thesis: UFC deal is transformative — secures most valuable live sports content in fastest-growing demo (18-34). Elimination of PPV in favor of Paramount+ subscription drives massive subscriber adds. Stock's 37% surge reflects initial re-rating but deal's long-term value changes Paramount+ value proposition fundamentally. Post-Skydance merger execution being validated by management's aggressive content strategy. In streaming wars, content-rich platforms win. Momentum continuation likely as analyst upgrades flow.
recommendations.catalyst: $7.7B exclusive UFC media rights deal (announced Aug 11). Eliminates PPV for Paramount+ subscribers. Stock +37% on Aug 13. $1.1B AAV over 7 years. First major content play post-Skydance merger.

recommendations.thesis: Energy is worst-positioned sector. Bearish confluence: OPEC+ abandoning production discipline a year early, US production at all-time highs, EIA forecasting sub-$60 oil by Q4, growing global inventories. CPI-driven rally in other sectors makes energy's relative underperformance stark — money rotating OUT of energy into rate-sensitive plays. WTI in low $60s pressuring E&P margins. Fresh EIA forecast (released Aug 12) is institutional intelligence driving selling. If PPI soft tomorrow, rate-cut narrative strengthens further — bearish for commodities.
recommendations.catalyst: EIA Aug 12 STEO forecasts Brent below $60 by Q4. OPEC+ unwinding 2.2mb/d production cuts by September (year early). US production at record 13.6mb/d. Oil -1.6% on Aug 13. Supply glut accelerating.
